text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The international community came to the rescue of financially strapped Thailand, pledging a total of S$23.5 billion in loans from the International Monetary Fund and Asian nations led by Japan.
- A "Division of work" would be one of Asean's strategies in its efforts to help restore political stability in Cambodia.
- The Dhoby Ghaut interchange, with five underground levels, will be the biggest station in the entire MRT network, moving 20,000 people in an hour during peak periods.
- The blue-chips Straits Times Industrials Index fell 2.6 percent to its four-year low, along with regional bourses spooked by currency volatility and Friday's Wall Street decline.
- Hong Kong has rejected former Merrill Lynch banker Kevin Wallace's application to travel to Singapore to face a court cross-examination on his assets, says his Singapore lawyer.

- Productivity gains that were stronger than expected helped Singapore Power record a 42.8 percent jump in net profit to S$771 million for the year ended March 1997, giving it returns which could justify a public listing.

- The increase in the Central Provident Funds minimum sum was not a cause of the S$14 million losses incurred by members who used their funds to buy insurance policies under the Enhanced Investment Scheme in the past three-and-a-half years, the CPF Board said.
- The Malaysian ringgit fell eight sen or almost 3 percent in Asian trading to close at 2.7350 to the US dollar compared with Friday's 2.6550 close.
- The management committee of the Real Estate Developers' Association of Singapore closed ranks behind president Heng Chiang Meng, surprising those who thought Mr Heng would be forced to step down.
- Vickers Ballas is continuing its strong profit run -- driven by the vibrant Hongkong stock market where the group is said to be planning a secondary listing.
- The Marco Polo hotel on Tanglin Road will stop operating in January 1999 to make way for condominiums expected to reap S$760 million in sales for Marco Polo Developments.
- Foreign share prices continued a general retreat, in some cases further narrowing their recent premiums over local share prices.
- Hotung Investment Holdings shares more than doubled in their trading debut on the Singapore exchange.
- Shares of Hotel Properties Ltd, a property and theme restaurant group, fell for a third day on profit concerns.
